pathway.title: GFL Environmental Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Earnings quality rests on price rather than volume, and it has held. Price added 5.7 percentage points to the 7.4% organic growth of the third quarter, 77.0% of it, while volume subtracted 0.1 percentage points, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.5% against 31.6% a year earlier, so margin is protected by pass-through pricing as long as price keeps pace with costs. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation F4

- Leverage is the central weakness and it rose fast. Net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA moved from 3.70x at the end of 2025 to 5.04x at the end of September, because net debt grew 55.0% while trailing Adjusted EBITDA grew 13.7%. Management reports 3.8x only after adding CAD 730.9 million of estimated run-rate earnings, and even on the midpoint of full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance net debt at September is 4.56x, so deleveraging depends on acquired earnings and savings that the filed figures do not yet show. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F5

- Cash flow after investment is thin. Operating cash flow of CAD 950.1 million for nine months left CAD 37.3 million after capital expenditure of CAD 912.8 million. The issuer's Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million is CAD 447.6 million higher because it adds back CAD 231.3 million of cash costs, counts CAD 33.9 million of disposal proceeds and leaves out CAD 182.4 million of incremental growth investments. Net new debt of CAD 2,972.0 million funded business acquisitions of CAD 2,569.8 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation F3

- Liquidity cannot be measured. Cash was CAD 296.5 million and the revolving credit facility was drawn CAD 868.0 million at 30 September, 42.9% of the two revolving facilities and up from CAD 182.0 million at 30 June, while letters of credit outstanding were CAD 535.1 million; undrawn availability is not stated, so runway against the 2028 maturities is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_tm2619744d3_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 10; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation F6

- Refinancing risk is back-ended but concentrated. Only CAD 14.2 million of debt falls due within twelve months and no note matures before 2028, but the 2028 notes of CAD 2,128.2 million are 19.1% of laddered principal and 43.3% matures by 2030. The cash flow statement shows CAD 6,795.9 million of long-term debt issued in nine months, including a Term Loan B Facility due 2033, so lenders have funded the acquisition programme so far. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; calculation F3; calculation F7

- Covenant and ownership uncertainty sit on top of the leverage. The revolver tests Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA at no more than 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x at other times, with compliance stated but no headroom or definition supplied, and governance risk is Medium because voting control is not disclosed and a take-private review is open. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1

cells.text: Non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill and material recovery, with industrial waste processing and disposal after SECURE
Facilities across Canada and 19 U.S. states; management calls GFL the fourth largest diversified environmental services company in North America
More than 17,000 employees in the third quarter release, up from more than 15,000 in the first and second quarter releases (management statements)
Canada and USA operating segments with a Corporate cost centre; Solid Waste is the segment subtotal
Collection 60.9% of gross revenue, landfill 14.9%, transfer 12.3%, material recovery 6.3%, other 5.6%
Organic growth 7.4%: price 5.7%, surcharges 1.5%, volume -0.1%, commodity price 0.3%; acquisitions 18.7% and foreign exchange 1.1%; reported growth 27.2%
Adjusted EBITDA margin 31.5%; Canada 35.7%, USA 33.8%; 31.6% in Q3 2025
Purchase of property and equipment CAD 912.8 million for nine months 2026, 15.9% of revenue; landfill assets CAD 2,547.7 million at 2026-09-30
Closure and post-closure obligations CAD 1,503.8 million at 2026-09-30, with funded post-closure trust assets of CAD 38.9 million
13 businesses acquired in nine months besides SECURE; management says completed acquisitions year to date generate about CAD 2 billion of annualised revenue
Not supplied: no source states customer concentration, municipal contract terms or renewal rates
The first quarter 2026 release cites unusually challenging weather; no seasonal split is stated

cells.text: Reported; includes 69.6 of discontinued operations in nine months 2025; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4

runs.text: Strength: pricing power across the network. Price added 5.7 percentage points to third-quarter organic growth while volume was flat to slightly negative, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 31.5%, so the network can pass cost inflation to customers and keep margin, which supports cash interest cover of 4.70x on nine-month Adjusted EBITDA and the ability to service the larger debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation F4; calculation F13

Strength: equity-funded growth and a distant first maturity. Shares paid 80.1% of the SECURE consideration, so the largest deal added less debt than a cash purchase, the issuer entered a Term Loan B Facility due 2033 in August 2026, and the first note maturity is in 2028, which limits near-term refinancing pressure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 13

Strength: scale and diversification inside waste. Collection is 60.9% of gross revenue with landfill, transfer and material recovery behind it, and revenue is 66.6% from the United States and 33.4% from Canada, so no single service line or country drives all earnings, although customer concentration is not disclosed. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation F9

Weakness: leverage rising faster than earnings. Net debt grew 55.0% since December 2025 against 13.7% for trailing Adjusted EBITDA, so the filed leverage of 5.04x depends on acquired earnings to fall, and any shortfall leaves less room under a covenant that returns to a lower level after four quarters. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation F1; calculation F2

Weakness: thin free cash flow and unmeasurable liquidity. Operating cash flow barely exceeded capital expenditure, the adjusted measure adds back cash costs the issuer expects to incur again, and undrawn availability is not stated, so the group depends on lenders and the revolver to fund acquisitions and the 2028 maturities. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation F3; calculation F6

Weakness: open ownership and event risk. Voting control is not disclosed, a special committee is reviewing take-private proposals with a deadline of 9 November 2026, and change-of-control terms are not supplied, so a leveraged transaction could raise debt or change creditor terms before any financing is visible. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The largest transaction is the purchase of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp., an operator of waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota. GFL agreed to buy all of its common shares on 2026-04-12 for shares and cash, SECURE shareholders approved in May, and the purchase closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of about CAD 5,414.1 million, made up of CAD 4,334.8 million of subordinate voting shares and CAD 1,079.3 million of cash. The allocation is provisional, with CAD 4,968.1 million of goodwill, and a nominee of SECURE joins the board, which rises to nine directors. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2612685d3_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-29_tm2619744d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2

Outside SECURE, GFL acquired 13 businesses in nine months 2026 for total consideration of CAD 1,598.5 million, of which CAD 1,413.7 million was cash, CAD 156.3 million shares and CAD 28.5 million contingent consideration. After 2026-03-31 it completed five further acquisitions for a combined purchase price of CAD 1,437.6 million. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2612685d3_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 15

New debt in 2026 comprises the senior notes due 2034, which first appear on the balance sheet at 2026-03-31 at CAD 1,393.9 million; the senior notes due 2031 that first appear at 2026-06-30 at CAD 1,065.8 million and were swapped on 2026-06-25; and a Term Loan B Facility entered on 2026-08-28 that matures on 2033-08-28 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at CAD 1,418.8 million at 2026-09-30 and swapped to a fixed rate on its date. The revolving credit agreement was amended and restated through 2026-09-01 and matures on 2030-04-29. The notes' issue dates are not stated; the dates above are the first balance sheets that carry them. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2612685d3_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_tm2619744d3_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 18

Capital returns and exits shape the perimeter. GFL completed the sale of GFL Environmental Services effective 2025-03-01, kept an option to repurchase the balance of its equity with a fair value of CAD 95.0 million at 2026-09-30, and accounts for its remaining interest by the equity method. The board received unsolicited preliminary expressions of interest to take the company private, and its special committee set a final deadline of 2026-11-09 for updated proposals. Share repurchases under the normal course issuer bid were 300,000 shares in nine months 2026. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-30_tm2626649d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 16; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-29_tm2619744d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-10-28_tm2626649d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen through 2026 because the balance sheet absorbed acquisitions faster than trailing earnings grew. On trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, net debt over EBITDA was 3.70x at the end of 2025, 3.90x in March, 4.45x in June and 5.04x in September. The issuer's own Net Leverage was 3.4x, 3.6x, 4.0x and 3.8x on the same dates, because its Run-Rate EBITDA adds management estimates of acquisition and cost-saving earnings, CAD 730.9 million at September. Until those earnings appear in reported results, creditors carry the filed figure, and the covenant test of Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA, set at 5.00 to 1.00 for four quarters after a Material Acquisition, is defined in an agreement that is not supplied, so headroom is not inferred. Against this, nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose 18.4% and the issuer states compliance with both maintenance covenants at 30 September 2026.

The year-to-date basis is used because the 2025 cash flow statement is not in the sources, so no trailing twelve months cover can be built.

The issuer's Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million adds CAD 231.3 million of cash costs to operating cash flow and CAD 182.4 million of incremental growth investments, which is why it is far above the simple measure. Capital expenditure is not split into maintenance and growth in the statements.

fields.value: Cash was CAD 296.5 million and the revolving credit facility was drawn CAD 868.0 million at 30 September 2026, up from CAD 182.0 million at 30 June. Letters of credit outstanding were CAD 535.1 million, of which CAD 187.8 million sat under the EDC facility. No source states undrawn availability, so liquidity cannot be measured. The debt note shows no note maturity before 2028; the only amount due within twelve months is the current portion of CAD 14.2 million, and the 2028 notes of CAD 2,128.2 million are the first wall, with the other facilities of CAD 528.0 million maturing in 2028 and 2030. The Term Loan B and the senior notes due 2031 and 2034 first appear in 2026, which lengthened the ladder while raising its total.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The SECURE acquisition closed on 1 September 2026 for total consideration of CAD 5,414.1 million, of which CAD 4,968.1 million is provisional goodwill, so asset, goodwill and deferred tax figures can still move. The 2025 comparatives were revised for associate adjustments, which changed total assets at the end of 2025 by CAD 92.7 million without touching debt or cash. Statement cells that the filings print as a dash are carried as not supplied rather than as zero. No non-debt funding float of size was found in the statements. Events after the balance-sheet date are flagged with their dates in the entity table and are not blended into period figures.

fields.value: - The FY2025 income statement and cash flow statement are not in the sources, which blocks trailing twelve months reported EBITDA, trailing twelve months cash interest and every fiscal-year ratio on reported figures. fields.value: - No source states undrawn committed facilities or total liquidity, and the split of letters of credit between the revolver and other facilities is printed only for the EDC facility, so cash plus undrawn facilities is not calculable at any date. Severity High. Action: obtain the liquidity table from the MD&A or the credit agreement.

The facilities left out are the revolving credit facility, the Term Loan B, the secured notes due 2028, the formerly secured notes due 2031, the senior notes due 2028, 2029 (two issues), 2031, 2032 and 2034, the tax-exempt bonds and the other facilities of non-wholly owned subsidiaries. fields.value: GFL Environmental Inc. (issuer id gfl), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, transaction, ownership, operating model and governance facts for the issuer and its consolidated subsidiaries that matter to a creditor, from the supplied annual report cover, interim statements and earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: GFL is a scaled, price-led North American waste operator whose creditors now face an acquisition-transformed borrower and an unresolved take-private review, so governance risk is Medium and control is not established. Collection supplied 60.9% of gross revenue for nine months and price added 5.7% to third-quarter growth, so earnings depend on pricing more than on volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity funded 80.1% of the CAD 5,414.1 million SECURE consideration, which eased the debt load of the deal, but ownership percentages, voting control and the outcome of the review after the 9 November 2026 deadline are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Growth is price-led and acquisition-fed. Organic growth was 7.4% in the third quarter, of which price contributed 5.7% and volume subtracted 0.1%, and acquisitions added a further 18.7%, so the reported 27.2% overstates the base business. Price is the mechanism that protects margin when volumes are flat, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% shows no erosion against 31.6% a year earlier, which supports debt service from the existing network.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The SECURE acquisition changed scale, mix and the claims against the business. It closed on 1 September 2026 and brought industrial waste processing and disposal in Western Canada and North Dakota into the group; Canada rose to 35.9% of third-quarter revenue from 33.0% a year earlier, and 91.8% of the consideration is provisional goodwill, so the asset base that backs the claims can still be restated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Equity funding makes the deal creditor-friendlier than its size suggests, but acquisitions overall were still debt-financed at the margin. Shares were 64.0% of nine-month acquisition consideration, while long-term debt issuance exceeded repayments by CAD 2,972.0 million and cash paid for acquisitions reached CAD 2,569.8 million, so leverage rose even though the largest deal was mostly paid in shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control and ownership cannot be established from the sources. A class of multiple voting shares exists, 2.71% of basic shares by count, but its holders, votes per share and the voting weight of the preferred shares are not disclosed, so whether a founder, a holder group or a dispersed base decides a sale or a recapitalisation is unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Related-party and leakage items are small but recurring. Cash payments to the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of CAD 74.2 million for nine months, which replaced payment in restricted share units, are 4.2% of Adjusted EBITDA and are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow, so adjusted measures overstate cash left for creditors by that amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The take-private review is the main event risk. Unsolicited proposals led the board to form a special committee of independent directors that set a final deadline of 9 November 2026, and GFL says no transaction is assured. A leveraged buyout would raise debt and could trigger change-of-control terms that the sources do not describe, so creditors cannot size the exposure yet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that equity paid most of the SECURE price, the third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 31.5%, nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose 18.4%, the issuer reports covenant compliance, and independent directors run the review. Share repurchases were also small in 2026, at CAD 71.0 million of cash for nine months against CAD 2,758.5 million in the same period of 2025. The view would improve if the voting control of the multiple voting shares were disclosed as dispersed or aligned with creditors, if the SECURE earnings and integration costs were shown in a full quarter, and if the review ended without a leveraged transaction. It would worsen if a bidder financed a purchase with new secured debt, if change-of-control terms were triggered, or if acquisition spending continued to be funded by net new debt rather than shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The largest transaction is the purchase of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp., an operator of waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota. GFL agreed to buy all of its common shares on 2026-04-12 for shares and cash, SECURE shareholders approved in May, and the purchase closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of about CAD 5,414.1 million, made up of CAD 4,334.8 million of subordinate voting shares and CAD 1,079.3 million of cash. The allocation is provisional, with CAD 4,968.1 million of goodwill, and a nominee of SECURE joins the board, which rises to nine directors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Outside SECURE, GFL acquired 13 businesses in nine months 2026 for total consideration of CAD 1,598.5 million, of which CAD 1,413.7 million was cash, CAD 156.3 million shares and CAD 28.5 million contingent consideration. After 2026-03-31 it completed five further acquisitions for a combined purchase price of CAD 1,437.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in 2026 comprises the senior notes due 2034, which first appear on the balance sheet at 2026-03-31 at CAD 1,393.9 million; the senior notes due 2031 that first appear at 2026-06-30 at CAD 1,065.8 million and were swapped on 2026-06-25; and a Term Loan B Facility entered on 2026-08-28 that matures on 2033-08-28 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at CAD 1,418.8 million at 2026-09-30 and swapped to a fixed rate on its date. The revolving credit agreement was amended and restated through 2026-09-01 and matures on 2030-04-29. The notes' issue dates are not stated; the dates above are the first balance sheets that carry them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns and exits shape the perimeter. GFL completed the sale of GFL Environmental Services effective 2025-03-01, kept an option to repurchase the balance of its equity with a fair value of CAD 95.0 million at 2026-09-30, and accounts for its remaining interest by the equity method. The board received unsolicited preliminary expressions of interest to take the company private, and its special committee set a final deadline of 2026-11-09 for updated proposals. Share repurchases under the normal course issuer bid were 300,000 shares in nine months 2026.

fields.value: GFL Environmental Inc. (issuer id gfl), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit view of the issuer and its consolidated subsidiaries, synthesised from the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules and the supplied filings, in Canadian dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: GFL's business quality is steady but its balance sheet is stretched: net debt reached 5.04x filed trailing Adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026 after SECURE, and liquidity cannot be measured, so the credit depends on acquired earnings arriving.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price added 5.7 percentage points to third-quarter organic growth and the Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 31.5%, which supports cash interest cover of 4.70x for nine months. Against that, net debt rose 55.0% since December 2025 while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.7%, free cash flow after capital expenditure was only CAD 37.3 million, and the take-private review leaves ownership and financing open. The primary downside is acquired earnings falling short before the first maturities arrive in 2028.

fields.value: - Covenant and ownership uncertainty sit on top of the leverage. The revolver tests Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA at no more than 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x at other times, with compliance stated but no headroom or definition supplied, and governance risk is Medium because voting control is not disclosed and a take-private review is open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better credit is operating momentum and a guided deleveraging path. Management reports underlying margin expansion of 115 bp excluding acquisitions and diesel prices, nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose 18.4%, equity paid 80.1% of the SECURE price, Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.70x, the issuer reports covenant compliance, and guidance puts net leverage in the mid 3s by the end of 2026. The guided path also requires fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about CAD 744.1 million, 9.6% above the third quarter, which a full quarter of SECURE, owned only from 1 September, could explain, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of about CAD 535.1 million against CAD 272.5 million in the third quarter, nearly double, so delivery is not yet evidenced. The view would improve if a full quarter shows SECURE earnings at the run-rate management assumes, if undrawn availability is disclosed as ample, and if the review ends without a leveraged transaction. It would worsen if price growth fell below cost inflation, if the Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped below the 31.5% of the third quarter, if revolver drawings kept rising, or if a bidder financed a purchase with new debt.

fields.value: GFL collects, transfers, landfills and recycles non-hazardous solid waste across Canada and 19 U.S. states, and added industrial waste processing and disposal in Western Canada and North Dakota when it acquired SECURE on 1 September 2026. Revenue is 66.6% from the United States and 33.4% from Canada for nine months, and collection supplies 60.9% of gross revenue. Management describes GFL as the fourth largest diversified environmental services company in North America, a self-description without share data. Collection and disposal are routine services, so revenue visibility is likely to be good, but the sources state no contract terms, renewal rates or customer concentration, so revenue durability beyond price is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are supported by revenue of CAD 5,746.9 million for nine months and a footprint across two countries, but market share is not stated. Competitive advantage is evidenced only by management's claim of industry leading organic growth and by landfill assets of CAD 2,547.7 million, so it is not established independently. Diversification is moderate by service line, and by customer it is not established. Cost and capex flexibility is limited by capital expenditure at 15.9% of revenue with little split between maintenance and growth. Margin stability is good on the issuer's adjusted measure, with 31.5% in the third quarter, but the reported EBITDA margin for nine months was 20.9% against 30.4% adjusted, because adjustments add back 45.3% of reported EBITDA. Free cash flow stability is weak, with CAD 37.3 million after capital expenditure. Ability to refinance is supported by CAD 6,795.9 million of debt issued in nine months and a first note maturity in 2028. Liquidity is not assessable because undrawn availability is not stated. Financial policy and governance is mixed: equity funded most of SECURE, but nine-month acquisitions were funded by net new debt, and ownership and take-private terms are open. Claims outside net debt add CAD 705.0 million of lease obligations and CAD 1,503.8 million of closure and post-closure obligations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is toward higher leverage and a larger, more acquisitive group. Total debt rose CAD 4,248.8 million, 57.2%, since the end of 2025 to CAD 11,671.4 million, and filed leverage falls only if acquired earnings and run-rate savings arrive. The main supports are price-led margin stability, equity-funded acquisition capacity and distant maturities; the main constraints are leverage, thin free cash flow after investment, unmeasured liquidity and an open ownership question.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the guided path is supportive but unproven: management raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to CAD 2,490 million to CAD 2,495 million, Adjusted Free Cash Flow to about CAD 1,020 million and says net leverage will be in the mid 3s by the end of 2026, with cash interest of about CAD 455 million. These figures include acquisitions completed as of 1 October 2026, net of divestitures, and assume an exchange rate of 1.40 Canadian dollars per US dollar. Tailwinds are continued price growth and a full quarter of SECURE earnings; the release names diesel prices as an incremental headwind and assumes no change in fuel and commodity prices, so a move in either is a risk to the guided margin. Over three to five years the sources state no dated target or leverage goal: management points to base-business margin expansion and higher free cash flow conversion, so the medium-term view is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with acquired earnings and price growth disappointing together. If SECURE and the 2026 acquisitions deliver less than the CAD 730.9 million of run-rate earnings management assumes, and price growth slows below cost inflation while volume stays flat, the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% would compress. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA would then stay near the filed level while cash interest, guided at about CAD 455 million for the year, and capital expenditure absorb operating cash flow, leaving free cash flow near the CAD 37.3 million seen for nine months. Leverage would stay above 5x on the filed basis, the revolver drawings of CAD 868.0 million would rise to cover acquisitions and interest, and if SECURE counts as a Material Acquisition the covenant level of 5.00x falls to 4.50x after four quarters, a definition the sources do not supply. The first maturities, the 2028 notes of CAD 2,128.2 million, would then need refinancing from a weaker position. Management levers are slowing acquisitions, funding them with shares as with SECURE, trimming growth spending of CAD 182.4 million and keeping share repurchases small, which were CAD 71.0 million for nine months. Resilience looks adequate through 2027 on maturity timing alone, because only CAD 14.2 million falls due within twelve months, but headroom against the covenant and undrawn availability are not established, so that conclusion is bounded. Observable triggers are price growth, organic growth, the margin, revolver drawings, the compliance statement and the outcome of the take-private review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, GFL presents an adequate business profile supported by price-led pass-through and a diversified service mix, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose to 5.04x on filed trailing earnings, thin free cash flow after investment and unmeasured liquidity. Against typical leveraged issuers in the sector the business is sound but the balance sheet is weaker, although no peer evidence is supplied to test that. Cash-flow durability appears adequate on the adjusted measure and weaker on reported figures. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on lender access and acquired earnings arriving before the 2028 maturities. The primary downside path is acquired earnings and price growth falling short while leverage stays above the covenant step-down. Further analysis would require the 2025 audited statements, undrawn availability, the debt documents and the outcome of the take-private review. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: leverage on filed earnings after the SECURE acquisition.
